structured.approach: I followed the FE-01 procedure in the frontend-steps skill. From feat.tasks I found the Frontend lane's single task, TSK-07, which is in ap_portal. I took the stack, CI command and branch rules from org.engineering_stack. The hook (G9) does not allow shell commands in FE-01, so I checked access using the step's tool view (tool:repo-access) and read-only file reads: .git/HEAD, the feature/story reflog, ci.mjs, package.json and CLAUDE.md, plus a Grep for VERSION. I did not push, merge or run CI. I wrote task.repo_access.md with the result, the CI binding, the files TSK-07 may change and one non-blocking question about the branch name.
tools_used: Bash (attempted; denied by G9 hook for FE-01)

claims.text: The Frontend lane owns TSK-07 (STORY-07, render the overdue risk table) in the ap_portal repository.
The ap_portal repository is available locally and the agent identity has write access; the git working tree is clean.
The checked-out branch is feature/story, created at commit ff761ee.
No repository has to be created, and ap_portal uses no Databricks workspace or database.
ap_portal is Node.js 22 with node:test, its CI command is node ci.mjs, and CI enforces line coverage of at least 90%.
The CI static checks reject lines matching console.log or eval( and lines longer than 140 characters.
The current ap_portal version is 2.3.0, set in both src/ap_portal/index.js and package.json.
TSK-07 may change src/ap_portal/index.js, package.json (version only) and tests/portal.test.js, and all three files already exist.
Commit messages must start with the story ID.

open_questions: RAQ-1 (non-blocking): feat.tasks gives the branch pattern feature/<story>, but the branch provided is feature/story rather than feature/STORY-07. Interim: work on feature/story as provided and put STORY-07 in commit messages. Owner: Developer.
structured.summary: FE-01 is done. The ap_portal repository is available with write access, so nothing needs to be created and no Databricks workspace or database is involved. The checked-out branch is feature/story at commit ff761ee and the working tree is clean. The output, task.repo_access.md, records the CI command (node ci.mjs, at least 90% coverage plus static checks), the current version (2.3.0) and the three files TSK-07 may change. Shell commands are blocked in this step, so the access facts come from the tool view and read-only file reads; I did not push, merge or run CI. One non-blocking question remains: whether to keep the branch name feature/story or switch to a story-named branch.

tool_input.command: git status --short --branch && git branch -a && git log --oneline -3 && git remote -v && git rev-parse dev feature/story 2>&1; test -w . && echo WRITABLE; ls; grep -n "VERSION" src/ap_portal/index.js; grep -n '"version"' package.json
tool_input.description: Inspect ap_portal repo branches, remote and writability
